prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the continuous 3D geometry of a tiled courtyard as the camera wearer steps out from behind an immediate doorway frame (<0.5 m on the right in frame 1) and walks forward between a row of three parked motorcycles on the left (1–3.5 m away, spaced ~0.8 m apart) and standing people on the right (1.5–4 m away). Across frames 1 to 3, a man in a grey suit (~2 m ahead, facing away from the camera wearer) walks toward a uniformed officer (~3.5 m ahead on the right, facing left) before passing out of view on the lower right as the camera wearer approaches the nearest blue and red motorcycles until they are within arm's reach (<1 m) in frames 3–5. In frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer's own extended right hand and held plastic cup appear brightly in the lower foreground (~0.4 m away, below eye level), while in frame 5 the wearer turns left toward a man in a blue patterned shirt (~1.8 m away, facing and looking toward the camera wearer) with three other men standing 2.5–4.5 m behind and to his right. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient makes the continuous ground-plane recession and the exact front-to-back layering of the overlapping motorcycles and the wearer's extended hand immediately quantifiable. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 1 where the near doorway saturates the dynamic range and renders the courtyard nearly black, and in frames 3–5 where background figures beyond 4 m fade into uniform darkness and thin motorcycle mirrors and handlebars blur into adjacent surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete object and person regions across the courtyard, separating the cluster of parked motorcycles on the left (1–3.5 m from the camera wearer) from multiple people distributed from 1.5 m to 6 m across the background and right side. In frames 1 and 2, it delineates the man in the grey suit (~2 m ahead, facing away) partially occluding the motorcycles to his left and the uniformed officer (~3.5 m away on the right), as well as three distant men (4–6 m away near the back wall, facing one another or sideways). As the camera wearer steps between the red and blue motorcycles in frames 3 and 4—bringing both bikes within arm's reach (<1 m) and cropping the surrounding people to their lower legs at the top and right edges—the masks track the shifting occlusion boundaries between the adjacent bikes. In frame 5, the map segments the man in the blue shirt (~1.8 m ahead on the left, facing and looking toward the camera wearer with the red motorcycle handlebars within his arm's reach), three men standing 1–2.5 m behind and to his right, and the plastic cup held in the camera wearer's hand (~0.4 m away at the bottom center). While segmentation clarifies instance boundaries in the crowded background and explicitly isolates the small translucent cup in frame 5 that blends into the tiled floor in RGB, it is unreliable where it mislabels the right doorframe as a surfboard in frame 1, fragments and drops the closer blue motorcycle entirely in frame 4, and fails to segment the camera wearer's arm or the red motorcycle in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map provides sparse 2D joint and keypoint locations on a black background, detecting only two foreground people and one egocentric hand across the entire five-frame sequence. In frame 2, a full-body yellow skeleton shows the man in the grey suit ~2 m in front of the camera wearer walking away with his back turned (shoulders level, head keypoints clustered at the back of the head, and right leg lifted ahead of the left) between the motorcycles on his left and the officer on his right. Frames 1 and 3 contain no pose detections at all because foreground figures are either heavily occluded by the doorway or cropped below the waist at the top and right frame boundaries as the camera wearer approaches the motorcycles. In frame 4, a magenta hand skeleton captures the camera wearer's own right hand extended ~0.4 m in front of the lens (within arm's reach of the red motorcycle's handlebars and mirror), and in frame 5, an upper-body yellow and magenta skeleton shows the man in the blue shirt ~1.8 m away to the left, facing and looking directly toward the camera wearer with his right elbow bent and right hand raised near his chest above the motorcycle within his reach. Although the skeletons clearly reveal the exact finger articulation of the wearer's cup-holding hand in frame 4 and the torso orientation and head-keypoint alignment of the two main individuals without visual clutter, the map is highly unreliable for overall scene layout because it misses all background people (2.5–6 m away), omits the wearer's hand in frame 5, and provides no representation of the motorcycles or environment.
